lede: Tuesday is the heavy lift this week: a newly seated Town Council takes up second reading of the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code, which would write new landscaping and historic-review standards into the Land Use Code — a vote that actually changes the rules here. The same day, the Housing Authority weighs a new primary-residency policy for dependents in multi-custodial households, and Thursday's Planning & Zoning session puts three Town-owned development projects, including the Carhenge redevelopment at 700 W Pacific, through subdivision and concept review.

notable.stake: Second reading vote on wildfire code changing landscaping and historic-review rules.
New residency policy for dependents in split-custody households could affect deed restrictions.
Three Town-owned projects, including Carhenge redevelopment, face subdivision and concept review.
